nodes.label: Failover Properties Reference
nodes.rationale: There are no mandatory properties — the framework starts with production-safe defaults.

nodes.label: failover.store.async + async-executor back-pressure
nodes.rationale: Writes (store/delete/cleanByExpiry) are offloaded to a virtual-thread executor while find is always synchronous because the caller needs the recovered value immediately. concurrency-limit + rejection-policy (DISCARD/CALLER_RUNS/ABORT) bound the blast radius; DISCARD is the default because the store is a regenerable cache.

nodes.label: failover.store.jdbc.strict-allowlist
nodes.rationale: Changed to true in 3.0.0: an empty resolved allowlist now denies all deserialization (fail-closed) instead of disabling the restriction. Affects only the degenerate case where nothing was discovered and nothing configured.

nodes.label: Observable properties (async publish, instance tag, cardinality guard)
nodes.rationale: Metrics publish off the caller thread via a bounded queue so emitting a metric can never block a @Failover call; a full queue drops the metric (counted) rather than back-pressuring. instance.mode=auto tags every registry except Prometheus (which adds instance at scrape). The cardinality guard caps distinct name values so a misconfigured name cannot explode the registry.

nodes.label: Dashboard properties (secure-by-default)
nodes.rationale: enabled defaults to false and is the only switch needed; exposure flags only narrow. allow-insecure is refused outright under the prod profile so production can never silently disable the access gate.

nodes.label: Dashboard cluster properties (local | prometheus | shared-store)
nodes.rationale: Peer-side snapshot.jdbc.enabled (direct write) is mutually exclusive with publish-url (HTTP push) and setting both fails fast at startup. Liveness needs both the dashboard-side and peer-side toggles because the dashboard cannot read a peer's config.

edges.source_location: both offload work to virtual threads with a bounded-queue/limit + drop-on-saturation policy
scatter concurrency-limit/rejection-policy mirror the async-executor guards
